column2: a brand new arched window, the whole window unit on its own: a fresh clean white painted wooden frame with a round arch over four whole panes of clear bright glass, the glass showing pale blue sky with one soft white cloud, a chunky new brass curtain rod carried on two round brass brackets across its top, two sunflower yellow curtains tied back neatly on both sides with plain round ties, and a chunky warm wooden sill running across its foot and returning a little way towards the viewer at each end.
column3: The window sits in the back wall, which stands square to the camera, so the whole unit is seen almost flat on: the frame's uprights are vertical, its arch is symmetrical, and only the thickness of its reveal shows, as a narrow band down the inside of its right hand edge, because the window lies a little to the left of the frame's centre. The sill crosses the foot of the window below the eye line, so its top surface is seen from above as a shallow parallelogram whose far edge is shorter than its near edge and whose right hand end runs away a little to the upper right.
column4: It is the height of a tall door and a little wider than a door: in the painted frame it stands about two fifths of the frame's width wide and a little over a third of the frame's height tall, with the arch's crown about a quarter of the frame's height down from the top. The curtains hang to just below the sill.
column5: The arch is symmetrical and the uprights are vertical, with the reveal showing only on the right hand side.

column2: a brand new chandelier hanging on a short straight chain: a chunky polished warm brass frame with three curved arms, each arm carrying a round warm cream glass shade that opens downwards, all three shades lit and glowing a soft warm yellow, hanging perfectly straight and level, with a round brass ceiling rose at the top of the chain.
column3: The chandelier hangs above the eye line, so it is seen from below: the ceiling rose at the top is seen almost edge on, the three arms spread out across the picture to the left and right, and each shade shows its open underside as a soft ellipse of glowing cream with the lit bulb inside it. The chain and the central column are dead vertical.
column4: It hangs near the middle of the room, a little right of the frame's centre: in the painted frame it spans about two fifths of the frame's width across its three arms and about a fifth of the frame's height from the ceiling rose to the bottom of the shades. The shades are a little wider than a grapefruit.
column5: All three shades are the same size and all three are lit, and the chain is vertical.

column2: a brand new fireplace with its chimney breast above it: smooth warm cream stone with no cracks, a chunky clean mantelpiece shelf, a swept clean hearth slab at its foot, and a cheerful fire burning inside on two logs, the flames big simple rounded shapes in sunflower yellow and warm orange glowing softly onto the hearth. Above the mantel a plain wooden picture frame hangs straight and level and holds a simple painting of a sunny green hill under a blue sky. A small green potted plant stands on the right hand end of the mantelshelf.
column3: The fireplace belongs to the right hand wall, which recedes away to the right, so the chimney breast turns its wide left hand face towards the camera and the viewer looks slightly along it: its front face is seen almost flat on while a narrow band of its left return shows down the left hand side, and all of its horizontal edges, the mantelshelf, the hearth slab and the top of the opening, run away to the upper right. The mantelshelf and the hearth slab both lie below the eye line, so both show their top surfaces as shallow parallelograms whose far edge is the shorter one.
column4: It is a tall structure running from the ceiling to the floor: in the painted frame it stands about a third of the frame's width wide across its breast and about two thirds of the frame's height tall, with the mantelshelf about a third of the way up from its foot. The hearth slab projects towards the viewer by about a quarter of the breast's width.
column5: The mantelshelf, the hearth and the top of the opening all run away to the upper right by the same angle.

column2: a brand new three seat sofa, chunky and rounded, upholstered in warm coral orange, with plump whole seat cushions and plump whole back cushions, two round sunflower yellow scatter cushions on it, generous rolled arms at both ends, and four short chunky wooden legs holding it level.
column3: The sofa stands against the back wall facing into the room, so it is seen almost from the front with its left hand end a little nearer the camera: its back and front are nearly parallel to the picture's horizontal, its left arm is the larger and sits a little lower in the picture, and its right arm is slightly smaller and sits a little higher as the body runs away to the upper right. It stands well below the eye line, so the viewer looks down onto it: the whole top of the seat cushions is visible as a band in front of the back cushions, and the top faces of both arms show.
column4: In the painted frame it stands about three fifths of the frame's width wide and about a quarter of the frame's height tall from the floor to the top of its back cushions. Its seat sits about one scatter cushion's height above the floor and the legs are short and stubby, about a third of the seat's thickness.
column5: The seat cushions show their top surfaces, and the right hand end sits slightly higher in the picture than the left.

column2: a brand new oval rug lying flat, whole and soft, a plain warm cream centre with two plain wide flat bands around its edge, the inner band teal and the outer band coral, with a soft rounded edge all the way round, no fringe and nothing standing on it.
column3: The rug lies flat on the floor well below the eye line, so it is seen from well above and strongly foreshortened: it reads as a wide oval, about half as tall in the picture as it is wide, with its long axis running across the picture and tilting very slightly up towards the right to follow the planks. Its near edge is the lower edge of the oval and is the thicker and more clearly seen one, and the whole rug lies in one plane with no part of it lifting.
column4: In the painted frame the oval spans about three quarters of the frame's width and about one fifth of the frame's height. Its thickness at the near edge is about a finger's width, showing as a thin soft band of its own darker tone under the coral border.
column5: It is one flat oval lying in the floor plane, wider than it is tall by about two to one, with no fringe.

column2: a patch of plain clean wooden floor and nothing else: wide warm honey brown planks laid side by side, swept clean and whole, with a few large clean butt joints across them and no object of any kind standing on it.
column3: The patch is the floor plane itself, seen from well above the eye line looking down: the long plank seams run from its lower left away towards its upper right, converging very gently as they go, and the short butt joints cross them the other way. The planks are wider at the bottom of the patch, nearest the camera, and narrow a little towards the top of the patch as they recede.
column4: The patch is a broad flat sheet of floor filling the whole frame, as wide as the room and about half as tall in the picture as it is wide, with about seven planks running across it. One plank is a little under a tenth of the patch's width.
column5: There is nothing standing on it and no shadow on it: it is only floor.

column2: a brand new flatscreen television standing on a low chunky television unit: a generous rounded flatscreen with a thin warm cream bezel and a dark softly glowing screen showing one simple bright shape, standing on a short chunky stand on top of a low two door cabinet in warm honey wood with two round brass knobs, and a small green potted plant on the cabinet beside it.
column3: The television unit stands on the floor in the near right of the room with its screen turned back across the room towards the sofa, so the viewer sees it from its front and a little from its right: the cabinet's front face is seen almost flat on with a narrow band of its right hand side showing, and its top, which lies well below the eye line, shows as a shallow parallelogram seen from above whose far edge is the shorter one and runs away to the upper right. The screen leans back very slightly with the stand and its top edge is seen from above as a thin line.
column4: It stands near the camera in the foreground, so it is drawn at a generous size: in the painted frame the whole unit is about a third of the frame's width wide and about an eighth of the frame's height tall, the cabinet taking the lower two fifths of that height and the screen the upper three fifths. The screen is about twice as wide as it is tall.
column5: The cabinet's top is seen from above and its far edge runs away to the upper right, and the screen faces back into the room to the upper left.
